Called 天後 in Li Bi's story of the melon poem.

Classical exemplar cited for gathering books. No personal name and no date in this passage.
Classical exemplar cited for understanding music. No personal name and no date in this passage.

Thirteenth son. Died very young at the beginning of Baoying.

Had twenty sons. The personal name is not given in this chunk.
Bore Dezong. Later sought as Empress Dowager Shen; this chunk gives no year for the search except that it precedes Shu's death in Zhenyuan 7.
Named as Empress Shen's son. This chunk does not give his birth order or accession year; 德宗朝 is his reign, before Shu's death.
Crown Prince Zhaojing, Prince of Zheng. The text gives no surname character.
Prince of Han, son of Empress Dugu. Enfeoffed at birth because his mother was favored. Died at forty-seven; the death year is not given. The draft romanizes 迥 as Hui.
Prince of Jun. Died young and was posthumously enfeoffed; no year is given.
Prince of Mu. Eldest of the princes in Dezong's reign.
Fifth son. Enfeoffed Prince of Chen (郴) in Dali 10, then Prince of Dan. Death is stated without a year. Not the later princes also romanized Yu.
Prince of Fu (鄜), retitled Prince of Jian in Jianzhong 4. The draft's Prince of Bin is 鄜, repaired to Fu. Death year not given.
Prince of Yi. The text writes the name 乃.
Prince of Sui. Not Li Yu the fifth son, nor the princes romanized Yu.
Prince of Jing. Died young. Posthumously enfeoffed in a first month; no year is given. The text gives no surname.
Prince of Shu. Original name 遂; renamed in Jianzhong 2. Not Shu, Prince of Mu.
Prince of Shao. Not Li Xian, Prince of Yan.
Prince of Duan. The draft also romanizes 逾 and 遹 as Yu.
Seventeenth son, Prince of Xun. Biography continues in the next chunk. Not the other men romanized Yu.
Eighteenth son. Not Li Tong, Prince of Ding.
Nineteenth son. Not Li Kui the chancellor.
Twentieth son.
Unnamed crown prince whom Prince of Zheng replaced as commander-in-chief in early Dali. This chunk does not name him.
Prince of Xun, seventeenth son. Death is not recorded here.
Prince of Gong, eighteenth son. Not Li Tong, Prince of Ding.
Prince of Yuan, nineteenth son. Not Li Kui the chancellor. Died in Dahe 6.
Prince of Ya, twentieth son. The death in the same sentence as the enfeoffment is not given its own year.
Filial son cited by the historiographer. No date.
Filial son cited beside Shen Sheng. No date.
The comment's ruler, who executed a beloved son and pardoned treacherous eunuchs. In this chapter's closing that is Suzong; the sentence gives no other name.
The encomium's advisor who moved his lord. The personal name is not given in this chunk.
The prince whose posthumous title the encomium praises. This sentence does not give a personal name; he is the beloved son of the preceding comment.
